topic: Hip fracture analgesia and nerve block

audits.title: A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF PAIN MANAGEMENT IN PATIENTS PRESENTING WITH HIP FRACTURE
audits.standard: Agency for Clinical Innovation (ACI) hip fracture minimum standard 2: pain management
audits.setting: Mona Vale Hospital, metropolitan hospital, Northern Sydney Local Health District

cycle1.result: Hourly pain scores on presentation in 82%; nerve blocks used in 35% in ED; 18% reported severe post-operative pain; neuropathic analgesia used in 14%; inappropriate NSAID use in 10%.

audits.other_findings: Analgesia prescribing varied; team developing a standardised pain pathway.
audits.citation: Gillespie H, Kwok A, Raves V, Bari A, Mestrov F, Rees T, et al.. A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF PAIN MANAGEMENT IN PATIENTS PRESENTING WITH HIP FRACTURE. Innov Aging. 2017;1(Suppl 1):869-869.

audits.title: PAIN-AGE, a Controlled Before/After Study Assessing an Audit and Feedback Perioperative Pain Management Intervention in Older Patients with Hip Fracture.
audits.standard: Receipt of acetaminophen 3 g/day during the three postoperative days, and nurses' adherence to medical prescriptions
audits.setting: Orthogeriatric unit (experimental group) with a conventional orthopaedic unit as control

cycle1.result: 16% of patients in the experimental group received 3 g/day of acetaminophen postoperatively before the intervention.

audits.intervention: Audit and feedback intervention built with nurses.

cycle2.result: 60% received 3 g/day of acetaminophen after the intervention; likelihood of receiving 3 g/day and prescription adherence significantly increased versus control.

audits.other_findings: 398 patients in total (mean age 89 years); functional status at discharge was better and length of stay shorter after the intervention.
audits.citation: Drevet S, Boussat B, Grevy A, Brevet A, Olive F, Richard M, et al.. PAIN-AGE, a Controlled Before/After Study Assessing an Audit and Feedback Perioperative Pain Management Intervention in Older Patients with Hip Fracture. . 2024. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-3978284/v1.

audits.title: Fascia Iliaca Compartment Block for Hip Fractures: Improving Clinical Practice by Audit.
audits.standard: NICE hip fracture guidance and BOAST fragility fracture analgesia guidance; local decision that all hip fracture patients receive FICB on presentation unless contraindicated
audits.setting: District hospital (Salisbury), emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics; NHFD data

cycle1.result: FICB administered in 45 (24.5%); mean post-FICB pain score 4 (NRS)

audits.intervention: Results discussed at departmental and Trust mortality meetings, one-to-one teaching on loss-of-resistance FICB for ED and T&O junior doctors, and enforcing completion of the hip fracture clinical proforma with FICB sign-off or documented contraindication

cycle2.result: FICB administered in 94 (44.3%) (p<0.00001); mean post-FICB pain score 3.6 (p<0.0011)

audits.other_findings: The text gives 148 patients in the first audit but the table gives n=184. No FICB complications were recorded; block success rate was 74%.
audits.citation: Okereke IC, Abdelmonem M. Fascia Iliaca Compartment Block for Hip Fractures: Improving Clinical Practice by Audit. Cureus. 2021;13(9):e17836. doi:10.7759/cureus.17836. PMID: 34660043.

audits.title: Perioperative pain management intervention in older patients with hip fracture in an orthogeriatric unit. A controlled before/after study assessing an audit and feedback intervention (PAIN-AGE).
audits.standard: Unit pain protocol: routine acetaminophen 1 g three times a day (3 g/day) during the three postoperative days
audits.setting: Orthogeriatric unit (experimental) versus conventional orthopaedic unit (control), Grenoble Alpes University Hospital; controlled before/after audit and feedback study

cycle1.period: December 2018 to April 2019 (before intervention, started May 2019)
cycle1.result: Postoperative 3 g/day acetaminophen 16% (16/99); preoperative 9%; nurse adherence to acetaminophen prescriptions 13% preoperatively and 13% postoperatively.

audits.intervention: Audit and feedback with nurses: two 1-hour pain teaching sessions, distribution of a pain assessment scale, protocol updated to 'give acetaminophen regardless of pain assessment', medicine staffing reviewed with clinical pharmacy, and night/weekend standby with a Saturday ward round.

cycle2.result: Postoperative 3 g/day acetaminophen 60% (60/100) (OR 8.55, p < 0.001; versus control OR 6.76, p < 0.001); preoperative 16% (p = 0.13); nurse adherence 32% preoperatively and 52% postoperatively.

audits.other_findings: Control unit showed no change (postoperative 29.3% to 33.7%). Intervention failed preoperatively; ADL at discharge improved and unit stay fell by 2.5 days, with no change in complications.
audits.citation: Drevet S, Boussat B, Grevy A, Brevet A, Olive F, Richard M, et al.. Perioperative pain management intervention in older patients with hip fracture in an orthogeriatric unit. A controlled before/after study assessing an audit and feedback intervention (PAIN-AGE). BMC Geriatr. 2024;24(1):735. doi:10.1186/s12877-024-05282-w. PMID: 39237920.

audits.title: Improving the rate of use of fascia iliaca compartment blocks in patients presenting with hip fractures.
audits.standard: Target fascia iliaca block in 50% of hip fracture patients within 18 months
audits.setting: Emergency departments, Royal University Hospital, Saskatoon (University of Saskatchewan)

cycle1.result: Baseline fascia iliaca block rate 2.0%; 6 physicians performing it.

audits.intervention: Three PDSA cycles: educational materials and standardised equipment carts; staff and trainee education sessions; further education, audit and feedback, and incentives.

cycle2.result: Fascia iliaca block rate 22.6%; 35 physicians performing it; special cause variation (shift) on SPC chart.

audits.other_findings: Target of 50% not met; one adverse event (arterial puncture) without significant harm.
audits.citation: O'Neill K, Boyle J, Haynes L, Ellis B, Woods R, Oyedokun T, et al.. Improving the rate of use of fascia iliaca compartment blocks in patients presenting with hip fractures. CJEM. 2026;28(1):27-33. doi:10.1007/s43678-025-00990-7. PMID: 40826210.

audits.title: Analgesia and Fascia Iliaca Compartment Block Utilisation for Neck-of-Femur Fracture Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.standard: NICE CG124 and RCEM guidance: FICB performed where applicable (100%); contraindications documented if FICB not performed (100%); pain re-evaluation within 30 minutes of analgesia (100%)
audits.setting: Emergency department, Macclesfield District General Hospital

cycle1.result: FICB performed 26/40 (65%); contraindications documented in 0/14 (0%) without FICB; pain re-evaluation within 30 min 21 (52.5%); mean time to first analgesia 130 ± 28.8 min; mean time to FICB 228 ± 36.2 min.

audits.intervention: Practical sessions to familiarise ED clinicians with FICB, and a mandatory analgesia checklist for all suspected neck of femur fractures (pain scores, analgesia times, FICB details and reason if not given).

cycle2.result: FICB performed 26/40 (65%, p=0.74); contraindications documented in 9/14 (64.3%); pain re-evaluation within 30 min 20 (50%, p=0.99); mean time to first analgesia 38.8 ± 13.2 min (p<0.001); mean time to FICB 63.4 ± 19.1 min (p=0.002).

audits.other_findings: FICB uptake and pain re-evaluation did not improve despite faster analgesia. No FICB-related complications in either cycle.
audits.citation: Ahmed T, Imtiaz H, Asghar R, Zaeem M, Monzur R, Jan AA, et al.. Analgesia and Fascia Iliaca Compartment Block Utilisation for Neck-of-Femur Fracture Patients: A Closed-Loop Audit. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e97771. doi:10.7759/cureus.97771. PMID: 41306811.

audits.title: Early fascia iliaca block documentation in hip-fracture care: A retrospective perioperative pathway audit.
audits.standard: Fascia iliaca block documented within 2 h of emergency department arrival
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust; operative hip-fracture pathway, retrospective audit

cycle1.result: 13 of 204 (6.4%; 95% CI 3.8% to 10.6%) had fascia iliaca block documented within 2 h.

audits.other_findings: 155 of 359 cleaned operative episodes (43.2%) had no recorded block timing category; mandatory timestamped recording and repeat audit recommended.
audits.citation: Mersal M, Moon Z, Ghauri AU, Purushothaman A, Elsaidy S, Ahmed KT, et al.. Early fascia iliaca block documentation in hip-fracture care: A retrospective perioperative pathway audit. J Perioper Pract. 2026. doi:10.1177/17504589261462323. PMID: 42500859.
